as_told.title: Puharich case of metal in teeth picking up signals

plain: A researcher named Greg Malatzi says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the scientist Andrija Puharich, working in a lab in New York in the 1950s or 1960s, met a mental patient who said he heard voices. According to the story, which Malatzi links to the journalist Annie Jacobsen, the man worked in a metal factory, and metal dust on his teeth was picking up the New York radio station WOR. Malatzi calls this Puharich's first "aha moment", since it hinted that the body could pick up signals directly.
